Subject: Planned maintenance: EU-West conservative driver sweep — opt-out and impact window

Hi Chris —

Quick heads up: we are scheduling a conservative driver sweep across EU-West to address a small number of telemetry-driven driver inconsistencies we observed in a limited host subset. Our goal is to keep customer impact minimal and avoid any forced cache invalidations. High level: 

- Window: Nov 9, 2026 22:00 — Nov 10, 2026 04:00 CET (6-hour rolling window across host pools)
- Expected customer-visible impact: nominal. We will prioritize hosts that are not in active low-latency pools; most requests will be routed to healthy variants.
- Opt-out: customers who need to skip this sweep for a particular pool can opt out by filling the short form below (deadline Nov 8, 18:00 CET).

Opt-out form: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/opt-out-euw-2026  (see related links)
JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721

Attachments: driver-sweep-checklist.pdf (short runbook)

If you want us to exclude Acme Media's media-rendering pool, please reply with the pool id (or fill the opt-out form) and we'll confirm.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Program Manager, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Hannah / team —

Based on current rollout policy INF-4721 and the conservative sweep configuration, opt-outs are supported per-host-pool and will prevent the driver migration for 14 days (to give us time to validate stability). Notes: 

- Opt-out preserves kernel/driver pairing for the nominated pool for 14 days; after that we'll contact the customer before any forced change.
- KV cache warmups: we will enable prefix-preservation where feasible; however, if a host is drained (evicted) as part of the sweep, the in-memory KV will be lost. We'll attempt to warm caches proactively for opt-out pools via background pre-warm requests.
- Rollback / fallback: if any increased error rate is observed (>0.4% 5m aggregated), the sweep will pause automatically and we will revert to previous driver on affected hosts.

Action items for this thread: 
- @Hannah: confirm acme-media-render-3 is excluded on opt-out if Acme asks.
- @Priyom: prepare a brief KB on how we perform prefix-preservation and warmup (attach to customer update).
- @Neha: schedule on-call shadow for the window and grab runbook.

I'll open a staging patch to mark acme pools as opt-out candidates once we get the list.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Chris —

Thanks — we can exclude acme-media-render-3 if you confirm the pool id in the opt-out form or reply here with the id and I'll action it. Confirmations: 

- Opt-out will preserve your driver pairing for 14 days (not 72). After that we'll reach out before any change.
- We'll run background warmups for the excluded pool to minimize latency drift; however this does not guarantee in-memory KV persistence in the event of host-level evictions.

If you want us to fully exclude the pool from the entire sweep (recommended for customer-critical media rendering), please reply with pool id(s) by EOD Nov 8 CET or complete the form. I'll confirm once I've recorded your opt-out.

Attachments: opt-out-form.csv (please fill and return if you prefer)

Regards —
Hannah
